58.name: Sharks (large coastal group)

zones.label: Virginia marine waters (to 3 mi)
zones.bagNote: 1 recreationally permitted shark per vessel per trip (a non-boat shore angler gets the vessel limit per day)
zones.sizeNote: 54 inch fork length minimum; great, scalloped and smooth hammerhead 78 inch fork length minimum

notes: Closed May 15 through July 15 every year for blacktip, bull, great/scalloped/smooth hammerhead, lemon, nurse, spinner and tiger sharks.
The 1-per-vessel limit covers ALL permitted sharks on the boat combined (except bonnethead, Atlantic sharpnose and smooth dogfish), no matter how many anglers are aboard.
Hammerheads must be 78 inches fork length; all others in this group 54 inches fork length.
Land sharks whole: head, tail and fins attached. Rod and reel or handline only; circle hooks required with bait.
Federal waters beyond 3 miles follow NMFS HMS rules, which differ.

61.auditQuote: 2. Atlantic sharpnose, bonnethead, finetooth, blacknose, and smooth dogfish sharks are exempt from the recreational size limit described in this subsection. ... A. Recreational fishing vessels are allowed a maximum possession limit of one recreationally permitted shark, excluding smooth dogfish, per trip

62.name: Sharks (pelagic: blue, porbeagle, thresher)

zones.label: Virginia marine waters (to 3 mi)
zones.bagNote: 1 per vessel per trip (shares the single-shark vessel limit)

notes: Blue, porbeagle and common thresher are recreationally permitted year-round at 54 inches fork length, 1 per vessel.
Bigeye thresher, shortfin mako and longfin mako are PROHIBITED - do not confuse them with common thresher.
Federal waters beyond 3 miles follow NMFS HMS rules.
62.auditQuote: "Recreationally permitted shark" means any of the following species: ... Blue, Prionace glauca ... Porbeagle, Lamna nasus ... Thresher, Alopias vulpinus

63.name: Dogfish (smooth & spiny)

zones.label: Virginia marine waters (to 3 mi)
zones.bagNote: No size or possession limit

notes: No size or bag limit on smooth or spiny dogfish.
Smooth dogfish must be landed whole (head and fins attached); spiny dogfish are exempt from the head-and-fins rule.
Dogfish do not count toward the 1-per-vessel shark limit.
63.auditQuote: No size or possession limits apply to Dog Sharks. ... All sharks (All species except Spiny Dog Sharks) must be landed with head and fins attached

64.name: Sharks (recreationally prohibited)

zones.label: Virginia marine waters (to 3 mi)
zones.bagNote: Possession prohibited

notes: These 23 species may not be taken or possessed recreationally in Virginia. Most commonly encountered: sandbar, dusky, sand tiger, Atlantic angel, white, bigeye thresher and both makos.
Shortfin and longfin mako were added to the prohibited list (regulation amended May 2025); the MRC web table footnote about mako sizes is outdated.
64.auditQuote: "Recreationally prohibited shark" means any of the following species: Atlantic angel, Squatina dumeril; Basking, Cetorhinus maximus; Bigeye sand tiger, Odontaspis noronhai; Bigeye sixgill, Hexanchus nakamurai; Bigeye thresher, Alopias superciliosus; Bignose, Carcharhinus altimus; Caribbean reef, Carcharhinus perezii; Caribbean sharpnose, Rhizoprionodon porosus; Dusky, Carcharhinus obscurus; Galapagos, Carcharhinus galapagensis; Longfin mako, Isurus paucus; Narrowtooth, Carcharhinus brachyurus; Night, Carcharhinus signatus; Oceanic whitetip, Carcharhinus longimanus; Sand tiger, Carcharias taurus; Sandbar, Carcharhinus plumbeus; Sevengill, Heptranchias perlo; Shortfin mako, Isurus oxyrinchus; Silky, Carcharhinus falciformis; Sixgill, Hexanchus griseus; Smalltail, Carcharhinus porosus; Whale, Rhincodon typus; White, Carcharodon carcharias

65.name: American Lobster

zones.label: Virginia marine waters
zones.bagNote: No recreational possession limit printed in 4VAC20-110
zones.sizeNote: Carapace length 3-17/32 inch minimum, 5-1/4 inch maximum

notes: Measure carapace length: keep only 3-17/32 to 5-1/4 inches.
No landing of lobster February 1 through March 31.
Release egg-bearing and V-notched females; spearing lobsters is illegal; keep them whole on the boat.
65.auditQuote: It shall be unlawful for any person to possess any lobster less than 3-17/32 inches in carapace length or any lobster greater than 5-1/4 inches in carapace length ... E. It shall be unlawful to land lobster from February 1 through March 31. ... A. It shall be unlawful for any person to possess any berried female lobster ... C. ... to possess a V-notched female lobster. D. It shall be unlawful to possess a lobster that has an outer shell that has been speared.

66.name: Hybrid Striped Bass
aliases: striped bass x white bass hybrid

zones.label: Virginia inland waters (statewide)
zones.bagNote: 4 per day, striped bass and hybrids combined

zones.label: Buggs Island Lake/Kerr Reservoir incl. Staunton River to Leesville Dam and Dan River to Union St. Dam
zones.bagNote: Oct 1-May 31: 2 per day aggregate (20-26 inch slot); Jun 1-Sep 30: 4 per day aggregate, no length limit
zones.sizeNote: Oct 1-May 31: 20 to 26 inch slot; Jun 1-Sep 30: none

zones.label: Claytor Lake and tributaries
zones.bagNote: Sep 16-Jun 30: 2 per day aggregate, 20 inch min; Jul 1-Sep 15: 4 per day aggregate, no length limit

zones.label: Lake Gaston
zones.bagNote: 4 per day aggregate

zones.label: Smith Mountain Lake and tributaries incl. Roanoke River to Niagara Dam
zones.bagNote: 2 per day aggregate
zones.sizeNote: Nov 1-May 31: no fish 30 to 40 inches; Jun 1-Oct 31: none

notes: Hybrids share one 4-fish aggregate with landlocked striped bass statewide (20 inch minimum).
Kerr, Claytor, Gaston and Smith Mountain Lake each have their own seasonal slot or minimum - check the zone for the lake you are on.
66.auditQuote: Striped Bass - Landlocked Striped Bass and Landlocked Striped Bass X White Bass Hybrids ... 4 per day in the aggregate No fish less than 20 inches

67.name: Roanoke Bass

zones.label: Virginia inland waters (statewide)
zones.bagNote: 25 per day, rock bass and Roanoke bass combined

zones.label: Nottoway, Meherrin, Blackwater (Franklin Co. and Chowan), Falling and Smith rivers and tributaries
zones.bagNote: 5 per day, rock bass and Roanoke bass combined

notes: Statewide: 25 per day combined with rock bass, no size limit.
In the Nottoway, Meherrin, Blackwater, Falling and Smith river systems: only 5 per day combined and an 8 inch minimum.
67.auditQuote: Roanoke Bass 25 per day in the aggregate with rock bass No statewide length limits | Nottoway, Meherrin, and Blackwater (Franklin County), Blackwater (Chowan), Falling and Smith rivers and their tributaries | 5 per day in the aggregate (combined) with rock bass No Roanoke bass less than 8 inches

68.name: White Perch

zones.label: Virginia inland waters (statewide)
zones.bagNote: No daily limit

zones.label: Lake Moomaw
zones.bagNote: 10 per day

notes: No statewide limit on white perch.
Lake Moomaw: 10 perch per day.
68.auditQuote: Perch (yellow and white) No statewide daily limit No statewide length limit | Lake Moomaw 10 per day

69.name: Bowfin

zones.label: Virginia inland waters (statewide)
zones.bagNote: 5 per day Jul 1 - Apr 14; 1 per day Apr 15 - Jun 30

notes: Spawning-season limit: only 1 per day from April 15 through June 30; 5 per day the rest of the year.
Printed as its own row by DWR, separate from longnose gar (same limits).
69.auditQuote: Bowfin July 1 to April 14: 5 per day April 15 to June 30: 1 per day No statewide length limits

70.name: Grass Carp

zones.label: Virginia inland public rivers and streams (not public lakes/reservoirs)
zones.bagNote: No daily limit; harvested fish must be dead

notes: Legal to keep from public rivers and streams only - not from public lakes or reservoirs.
Every grass carp you keep must be dead before you leave the water.
70.auditQuote: Grass Carp No statewide daily limit No statewide length limit | Anglers may possess grass carp taken from inland public waters, except for public lakes and reservoirs. Anglers must ensure that harvested grass carp are dead.

71.name: Common Carp

zones.label: Virginia inland waters
zones.bagNote: No possession limit

notes: No limit on common carp.
If taken by bow, the fish must be kept, not thrown back or dumped on the bank.
71.auditQuote: No possession limits - can be possessed in unlimited numbers. Carp, mullet, white sucker, northern hogsucker, gizzard shad, threadfin shad, white perch, yellow perch (10 fish limit in Lake Moomaw), alewife and blueback herring [see limits under Anadromous (coastal) in creel and length limits table], stoneroller (hornyhead), fathead minnow, golden shiner, goldfish, and Asian clams.

72.name: Nongame fish (no possession limit)

zones.label: Virginia inland waters
zones.bagNote: No possession limit

notes: DWR lists these nongame fish as unlimited: carp, mullet, white sucker, northern hogsucker, gizzard shad, threadfin shad, white perch, yellow perch, stoneroller, fathead minnow, golden shiner, goldfish, Asian clams.
Alewife and blueback herring are listed here but are closed in all Chesapeake Bay coastal rivers and the Chowan drainage - see those rows.
72.auditQuote: No possession limits - can be possessed in unlimited numbers. Carp, mullet, white sucker, northern hogsucker, gizzard shad, threadfin shad, white perch, yellow perch (10 fish limit in Lake Moomaw), alewife and blueback herring [see limits under Anadromous (coastal) in creel and length limits table], stoneroller (hornyhead), fathead minnow, golden shiner, goldfish, and Asian clams.

73.name: Other nongame fish (20 per day)

zones.label: Virginia inland waters (statewide)
zones.bagNote: 20 per day

notes: Any native or naturalized nongame fish not listed as unlimited: 20 per day.
Bait minnows, chubs and hellgrammites: 50 combined unless you have a purchase receipt. Crayfish: 20 combined.
Suckers taken by dip net (Feb 15 - May 15) or by snagging/gigging in the listed southwest Virginia waters: 20 per day.
73.auditQuote: Other native or naturalized nongame fish 20 per day No length limits | Statewide | See pages 27-28 for exceptions

74.name: Threatened and endangered fish (no possession)

zones.label: Virginia inland waters
zones.bagNote: Possession prohibited

notes: No possession of any state or federally threatened or endangered species, freshwater mussels, candy darter or eastern hellbender.
Freshwater mussels may not be taken from any inland water in Virginia.
74.auditQuote: Threatened and endangered species No possession | None apply | None apply

75.name: Hickory Shad

zones.label: Meherrin (below Emporia Dam), Nottoway, Blackwater (Chowan), North Landing and Northwest rivers and tributaries, plus Back Bay
zones.bagNote: 10 per day

zones.label: Chesapeake Bay coastal rivers above and below the fall line
zones.bagNote: As set by VMRC for tidal rivers (no hickory shad rule printed on the VMRC recreational table)

notes: Chowan-drainage rivers (Meherrin, Nottoway, Blackwater, North Landing, Northwest) and Back Bay: 10 per day, no size limit.
Chesapeake Bay rivers: DWR defers to VMRC; VMRC's recreational table prints no hickory shad limit, so confirm with VMRC before keeping any.
Do not confuse with American shad, which is catch-and-release only statewide.
75.auditQuote: Hickory Shad - Above and below the fall line in all coastal rivers of the Chesapeake Bay and their tributaries: Creel and length limits shall be the same as those set by the Virginia Marine Resources Comm. in tidal rivers | Meherrin River below Emporia Dam, Nottoway River, Blackwater River (Chowan Drainage), North Landing and Northwest rivers, and their tributaries plus Back Bay: 10 per day No length limits

76.name: Southern Flounder

zones.label: Back Bay and tributaries incl. Lake Tecumseh, and North Landing River and tributaries
zones.bagNote: 6 per day

notes: Applies only in Back Bay, Lake Tecumseh and the North Landing River system (DWR waters).
Elsewhere in Virginia tidal waters follow the VMRC summer flounder rule (4 per person; 16 in Jan-May, 17.5 in Jun-Dec).
76.auditQuote: Southern Flounder - Back Bay and tributaries, including Brinson's Inlet Lake (Lake Tecumseh), and the North Landing River and its tributaries: 6 per day, no fish less than 15 inches

77.name: Crayfish

zones.label: Virginia inland waters
zones.bagNote: 20 in aggregate (all species combined)

notes: 20 crayfish total per person; they may not be sold.
77.auditQuote: The possession limit for crayfish is 20 in aggregate. Note: Madtoms, crayfish, and salamanders cannot be bought or sold.
